newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Progress made in S.African metal wage dispute.
newsitem.headline: Progress made in S.African metal wage dispute.

text.p: Progress has been made in resolving the wage dispute in the South African metal and engineering industry, an employer body said on Tuesaday.
The Steel and Engineering Industries Federation of South Africa (Seifsa) said this followed a meeting between employers and the industry's nine unions to discuss contentious issues.

"Some progress was made towards resolving the dispute in the industry's wage negotiations with employer and trade union representatives undertaking to reconsider their stance on a number of key issues," Seifsa said in a statement.
The parties agreed to a further meeting on July 15.
Wage talks reached deadlock on June 12 when unions rejected the employers' final wage offer of between eight and 8.5 percent together with other improved offers on conditions of employment.

A number of unions, including the Congress of South African Trade Unions-affiliated National Union of Metalworkers of SA and the Chemical Workers' Industrial Union, subsequently declared a dispute with employers.
Unions are demanding wage increases ranging from 13 to 23 percent.
